subject: Biotechnology
title: RNAi-Based Pest Control
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on RNAi-Based Pest Control.

hook.text: Spray RNA on crops and silence pest genes — RNA interference as a pesticide, no toxin needed.

buildup.text: Double-stranded RNA targeting an essential insect gene is absorbed when pests eat treated leaves.

discovery.text: The RNA triggers destruction of the pest's own messenger RNA — its vital proteins stop being made.

twist.text: Species specificity is a feature — RNA designed for one pest does not affect bees, butterflies, or mammals.

climax.text: Calantha's Ledprona is the first EPA-approved RNAi biopesticide — targeting Colorado potato beetle with RNA spray.

punchline.text: Silence pest genes with a spray — RNA pesticides target with molecular precision.

quiz.question: Why are RNAi biopesticides considered safer than chemical pesticides?
options: They evaporate before reaching the soil
They target specific pest genes without affecting non-target species like bees or mammals
They are made from organic materials that decompose instantly
